provider_modes.reconcilable: stable evaluation ID plus durable query-by-ID reconciliation; controller reconciles before any execute on restart
provider_modes.neither: no same-key idempotency and no reconciliation; any durable unresolved intent after restart is treated as UNKNOWN and cannot be replayed

tested_cases.recovery: reconcile found the already-committed provider effect; no second execute

tested_cases.interpretation: conservative false blockage is unavoidable once an unresolved intent cannot be distinguished from an accepted request

tested_cases.recovery: no execute and no reconcile on restart; uncertain evaluation remains UNKNOWN

bounded_inference: Within this local SQLite reference, crash-safe switching requires a provider recovery capability for automatic continuation. When the provider supplies neither durable idempotency nor reconciliation, the only safe generic restart rule after an unresolved dispatch intent is fail-closed UNKNOWN, even though this can conservatively block a request that in fact never left the controller.
scope_limit: Local SQLite controller/provider simulator only. It does not prove arbitrary network/provider semantics, and its UNKNOWN behavior is a safety policy rather than an exactly-once guarantee.
